title: Federated compute provisioning
subtitle: One call stands up GPU capacity on a local card, a LAN workstation over mutual TLS, or rented cloud spot capacity, behind a fail-closed daily budget.

stats.label: MCP actions on the node-management tool
lines of Rust in the provisioning substrate, across 26 files
providers behind one trait: local, LAN and cloud

lede: FAFO Core and Function Forge needed compute from wherever I had it: the workstation, a spare machine on the LAN, or a rented cloud GPU up to datacentre Blackwell. I made location a parameter of one MCP call. Underneath is one Rust provider trait, implemented for local Docker, LAN Docker daemons reached over mutual TLS, and RunPod for cloud pods. I kept one implementation of ports, health, events and spend, and every family of workloads composes it. I chose plain Docker with a provider trait and my own CA over Kubernetes. The dollar budget sits inside the provisioning call and only a person can set it.
quote: The estate is a handful of machines, and the scheduler I needed was a budget.
evidence: Cloud GPU provisioning with cost controls: one MCP call places capacity on a local card, a LAN host over mutual TLS or a cloud pod, behind a daily budget only a person sets, checked before anything exists.
Rust systems engineering: one provider trait with three implementations over shared port leases, health, events and spend, 17,303 lines across 26 files.
Zero-trust and zero-inbound networking: cloud pods dial back to the private network so no GPU host opens an inbound port, and LAN hosts join through an 11-step onboarding with rollback.
MCP server design: a node-management tool of 15 actions that reads each engine's declared token capacity, so cards of different sizes drain one backlog.
author: Corey James
